To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the growth of barley leaf lamina is a dynamic process that is characterized by the formation of a new cell wall at the tip and by the elongation of cells in the basal region.
the XET‐related genes in barley are involved in leaf growth and are differentially expressed during growth of the leaf lamina.
the XET‐related genes are expressed during leaf development and growth and that the XET activity is correlated with leaf growth.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanisms of the growth and differentiation of plant cells.
the development of new technologies to improve the quality and safety of food.
the molecular and genetic control of leaf growth in barley and other cereals, and the application of the knowledge gained to the development of new varieties with enhanced yield potential.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the observed growth kinematics in the leaf lamina are not only a consequence of the underlying growth of the leaf sheath, but that the leaf lamina also has an independent growth pattern.
XET‐related genes are expressed in barley leaves, but the expression patterns are complex and not necessarily related to cell wall loosening or growth.
the growth rate of the leaf is a function of the growth rate of each cell in the leaf.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown that there is a strong link between XET‐related genes, cell wall loosening, and growth.
the XETs are involved in cell wall loosening during the growth of leaves and roots and in cell wall thickening during the growth and development of the root.
XET-related genes are expressed in a tissue specific manner, with some genes expressed in all tissues, and others expressed only in specific tissues.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the genes that control leaf growth in the barley plant are not only expressed in the leaf but also in the root, and the genes that control growth in the root are also expressed in the leaf.
the XET‐related genes in barley are involved in the regulation of growth kinematics, and that this regulation is not limited to the cell wall but also involves cell turgor and cell volume.
the XET‐related genes are not involved in cell wall loosening, but in cell wall stiffening, which in turn affects the growth rate.
